title: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
summary: A two-dumbbell row lying face down on an incline bench, needing no machine and putting no load on the lower back.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.7 for lats (helper): each working set adds 0.7 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.6 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.55 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.55 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.
Library rating 0.45 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.45 of a set to the weekly biceps total.

setup.text: Lie chest-down on a bench at about 30 degrees with dumbbells hanging.
Row both dumbbells up until your elbows pass your torso.

form_cues.cue: Row the dumbbells toward your hips
Keep the chest on the pad
Keep your chest on the bench. Don't lift it to cheat.

mistakes.text: Lifting the head and chest off the bench.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less upper-back focus, Less stable, One side at a time.
Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Less upper-back focus, Less stable.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stable, Lower loading potential.
